title: The constant square-zero residue and its truncation counterexample
statement: Let ell be prime, k a separably closed field, X=Spec k, and Lambda the discrete continuous condensed ring A=Z/ell^2. Let P be the cokernel of ell times the identity of the regular condensed Lambda-module, and M its monoidal inverse image to X. Then M is constant-model constructible, M[0] has no finite Tor amplitude, and there exists a bounded constant-model constructible complex K of finite Tor amplitude such that truncGE_0(K) has no finite Tor amplitude. The assertion is invariant under a specified condensed coefficient-ring isomorphism, so it is stated for an abstract commutative condensed ring isomorphic to the continuous finite ring.

source.place: The examples, constant-sheaf specialization and the two-term truncation counterexample

proof.text: Set A = Z/ell^2. Prove ell^2=0 and ann(ell)=(ell) directly using ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff and cancellation of the positive prime in natural-number divisibility. The normalized finite-discrete canonicalAbelianMap is an isomorphism from the constant abelian sheaf A to the coefficient object. Compose with the given coefficient isomorphism. Constant abelian sheafification preserves exactness, and faithful exact forgetting from internal modules reflects it, so multiplication by ell on the actual internal tensor unit is square zero and its repeated short complex is exact. The constant-section map on the identity pro-etale object is injective: otherwise its equalizer sieve is the empty covering sieve, impossible on a nonempty scheme by joint surjectivity. This proves the tensor unit is nonzero. No derived coefficient transport is used.

In the internal monoidal abelian category construct the chain complex with unit terms and multiplication by ell as every differential. Exactness of the repeated short complex and the cokernel augmentation prove it is a resolution of F=coker(ell). Extend to nonpositive integer degrees. Every term is flat (unit or zero), so the bounded-above flat K-flat criterion applies. Ell annihilates F by cancellation against its cokernel epimorphism; naturality of the left unitor then shows that all differentials vanish after tensoring with F. The generic source QObjTensorSingleFunctorObjIso identifies this termwise tensor with F[0] tensor-derived F[0]. In every degree -q its homology is F. If F were zero then ell would be epic, its square-zero relation would force ell=0, and the tensor unit would be zero. Thus F is nonzero and its tensor homology contradicts any finite lower Tor bound.

The condensed cokernel has a finite presentation by a 1 by 1 matrix, using the one-summand finite-free/unit isomorphism and cokernel.mapIso. Its inverse image is canonically the internal cokernel F, since the additive point inverse image preserves cokernels and the regular module. On the singleton identity cover it is a finite constant local model. The trivial stratification proves constructibility on qcqs schemes; on every affine open pull back the local model and use the same trivial stratification. Constructibility transports across isomorphisms by its existing well-definedness theorem.

Construct the double complex [unit --ell--> unit] in degrees -1 and 0. Its two terms are flat, and the generic source bounded-flat Tor theorem gives amplitude [-1,0]. Compute its homology by the short-complex kernel/cokernel APIs: H^0 is F and H^-1 is ker(ell), isomorphic to coker(ell) using exactness and the image/coimage isomorphism. Every other homology is zero, which is also a finite constant model. Therefore its localization is bounded constructible. Its truncation in degrees at least zero is concentrated in degree zero. The single-degree derived-category theorem, homology preservation of truncGE, and the computation H^0=F give its isomorphism with F[0]. Isomorphism invariance transports the already proved infinite Tor amplitude to this truncation and to the displayed pulled-back module.

lean.statement:
theorem constant_square_zero_tor_example (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{0}) Ab.{1})
    [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ]
    (hΛ : Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅
      Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousCoefficientRingObj.{0} (ZMod (ℓ ^ 2)))))
    (k : Type) [Field k] [IsSepClosed k] :
    let X : Scheme.{0} := Scheme.Spec.obj (Opposite.op (CommRingCat.of k))
    let C := Mod (Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{0}) Ab.{1}) Λ
    let P := cokernel ((ℓ : ℕ) • (𝟙 (𝟙_ C)))
    let Cₓ := Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X)
    let M : Cₓ := ((upperStarFromPoint X).mapMod Λ).obj P
    IsConstantModelConstructible Λ X M ∧
    ¬ _root_.DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude Cₓ
      ((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor Cₓ 0).obj M) ∧
    ∃ K : DerivedCategory Cₓ,
      (constantModelBoundedConstructible Λ X ⊓
        _root_.DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude Cₓ) K ∧
      ¬ _root_.DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude Cₓ
        ((_root_.DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE 0).obj K)
